title: Trace normalization and transitivity
statement:
Work in the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], and put
$\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes,
let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type
morphisms of relative dimensions $d,e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$. The typed composite

$$
\begin{array}{l}
R(gf)_!L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]
\xrightarrow{\ \alpha_{g,f}^{-1}\ }
Rg_!Rf_!Lf^*Lg^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]\\
\hphantom{R(gf)_!L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]}
\xrightarrow{\ Rg_!(\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,Lg^*K(e)[2e]})\ }
Rg_!Lg^*K(e)[2e]
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{g,K}\ }K
\end{array}
$$

where $\alpha_{g,f}$ is the composition law of
[thm-sf-comp-composition],
equals $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{gf,K}$, after the pullback-composition
and twist-additivity identifications; thus the $f$-trace, with the
$(e)[2e]$ twist already present, is applied before the $g$-trace.
On every geometric fiber of a structural $f=p_d:\mathbf A^d\to\Spec k$,
the smooth trace

$$
\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{p_d,\Lambda}:
R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^d,\Lambda(d)[2d])\longrightarrow\Lambda
$$

is the product of the normalized affine-line traces of
[thm-pur-affine-line-purity]: it sends the ordered fundamental class
of $\mathbf A^d$, the $d$-fold tensor of the affine-line classes, to
$1\in\Lambda$. The smooth traces are compatible with arbitrary base
change of $Z$ and with the coefficient transports of
[thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity],
[thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], and
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity].

proof.text:
Work first at $A=A_{E,n}$, at an arbitrary positive level. Write $F_f=Rf_!$, $U_f=Rf^!$, $S_f=Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$, and similarly for $g$ and $gf$; write $\epsilon_f:F_fU_f\to1$ for the constructible counit. By [def-pur-smooth-trace], $t_{f,N}=\epsilon_{f,N}F_f(\gamma_{f,N})$. All adjunctions here are the constructible ones of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], without the optional ambient exceptional-adjoint hypothesis. The inputs $S_gK$ and $U_gK$ are in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] and [thm-sf-preservation-class], with shifts preserving that property and tensoring by the finite locally free Tate line preserving it by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Bounded constructible objects have the etale-origin witnesses of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so [thm-sf-comp-composition] applies to the displayed compact-support composites. Under its $\alpha$ and the conjugate comparison $c:U_{gf}\cong U_fU_g$, the counit is
$$\epsilon_{gf,K}=\epsilon_{g,K}\,F_g(\epsilon_{f,U_gK})$$
after identifying its source. Indeed [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] defines this pasted counit, and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] defines $c$ as the adjoint comparison that identifies it with the chosen counit for $gf$. Thus this equality concerns the actual composition comparison, not an arbitrary isomorphism between right adjoints.

source.place: Step 1: constructible adjunctions and their composition

proof.text:
Put $N=S_gK$ and $a=\gamma_{g,K}:N\to U_gK$. The maps $\gamma_{f,-}$ are natural: in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] the orientation is fixed, tensoring with its inverse is a natural transformation, and the specified tensor map is the adjoint transpose of a natural projection/counit composite. Consequently
$$\gamma_{f,U_gK}\,S_f(a)=U_f(a)\,\gamma_{f,N}.$$
Counit naturality gives $\epsilon_{f,U_gK}F_fU_f(a)=a\epsilon_{f,N}$. Substitute these two equations and the composition identity of [thm-pur-composition-coherence] into the preceding counit formula. After the source identification $F_{gf}S_{gf}K\cong F_gF_fS_fS_gK$, the result is
$$\begin{aligned}
t_{gf,K}
&=\epsilon_{g,K}F_g(\epsilon_{f,U_gK})F_gF_f(\gamma_{f,U_gK}S_f(a))\\
&=\epsilon_{g,K}F_g(a)F_g(\epsilon_{f,N}F_f(\gamma_{f,N}))\\
&=t_{g,K}F_g(t_{f,S_gK}).
\end{aligned}$$
This is the required transitivity, with $S_gK=Lg^*K(e)[2e]$, so the existing $(e)[2e]$ twist stays inside the input of the $f$-trace. No cancellation of a purity map with a counit, or triangle identity involving $\gamma$, was used.

source.place: Step 1: purity composition and counit naturality

proof.text: For the affine-line projection over the algebraically closed ground field $k$, use the actual normalized integration of [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement], which states its formula at every $n\geq1$: it is extension by zero into $q:\mathbf P^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, followed by the Kummer-normalized $t_q$. Its adjoint is the affine-line purity map, so applying compact support and then the counit recovers this integration by the inverse Hom bijection. The zero-divisor class in $H^2_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^1,A(1))$ is $\partial\kappa(t)$ and represents $1$ by [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]. Its compactly supported image maps on $\mathbf P^1$ to $c_1(\mathcal O(\{0\}))$ by [lem-pur-divisor-class]; this is $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$, since the zero point is a degree-one hyperplane. The class lies away from infinity, so the map to projective-line cohomology is precisely the extension-by-zero map in the definition of integration. By [def-amb-p1-trace], $t_qc_1(\mathcal O(1))=1$. Thus the smooth affine-line trace sends the specified normalized class to $1$. The comparison of the actual projective-line and affine-line maps in [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies this ordinary etale computation with the specified pro-etale Tate twist and counit; it is valid for any annihilator $\ell^rA=0$, without a ramification-divisibility hypothesis on $n$. For an arbitrary geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, pull back this equality: compact-support base change [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] identifies its source with the fiber compact-support object, and the arbitrary-base-change Cartier Kummer class of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies the pulled-back class with the normalized fiber class. Pullback takes the right-hand side $1$ to $1$, proving the same normalization on every such geometric fiber.

We prove the ordered affine-space normalization by induction on $r\geq0$. For $r=0$, [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] gives the identity purity map, and the identity adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] has identity counit: the empty tensor class maps to $1$. For the step write $p_{r+1}=p_rq_r$ with $q_r:\mathbf A^{r+1}\to\mathbf A^r$ the last-coordinate affine-line projection, as in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. The relative line class $c_{q_r}:A_{\mathbf A^r}\to Rq_{r!}A(1)[2]$ is the pullback of the one-dimensional class, using compact-support base change [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. The base-change compatibility of affine integration in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], and its equality with the pro-etale integration of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], give $I_{\mathbf A^r}c_{q_r}=1$. Under the natural projection isomorphism of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], the trace of $q_r$ with coefficient $M=A_{\mathbf A^r}(r)[2r]$ is $1_M\otimes I_{\mathbf A^r}$: this is the transpose formula in [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement]. Hence it sends $1_M\otimes c_{q_r}$ to $1_M$. The ordered external product class in dimension $r+1$ is obtained by applying $Rp_{r!}$ to this map from $M$ and precomposing the class in dimension $r$, with the composition comparison [thm-sf-comp-composition]. This is the coordinate-tower construction of the ordered tensor of the $r+1$ line classes; only the projection map is needed, not a separately assumed Kunneth isomorphism. Transitivity proved in Step 2 sends this class first to the $r$-dimensional class and then, by induction, to $1$. The purity comparison used is the ordered one by [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] and [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. Coordinate order is retained throughout; any shift reassociation has sign $(-1)^{(2r)2}=1$. This proves the stated normalization for every $d$, including $d=0$.

source.place: Step 2: ordered coordinate induction and the rank-zero case

proof.text:
Consider an arbitrary Cartesian base-change square with vertical map $h$ smooth separated, top map $u$, bottom map $v$, and base-changed vertical map $h'$. Write $B_M:Lv^*Rh_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh'_!Lu^*M$ for compact-support exchange, invertible on the relevant etale-origin objects by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Let $e_K:Lu^*Rh^!K\to Rh'^!Lv^*K$ be the adjoint transpose of $Lv^*(\epsilon_{h,K})B_{Rh^!K}^{-1}$. By the mate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate],
$$\epsilon_{h',Lv^*K}Rh'_!(e_K)=Lv^*(\epsilon_{h,K})B_{Rh^!K}^{-1}.$$
This is the counit-normalized exceptional base-change map; its unit-object form is explicitly specified in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. The orientation and tensor-map clauses of [det-sp-purity-bc-factors], applied to finite $A$, give
$$e_KLu^*(\gamma_{h,K})=\gamma_{h',Lv^*K}b_K,$$
where $b_K:Lu^*S_hK\cong S_{h'}Lv^*K$ is the pullback/twist/shift identification. Apply $Rh'_!$ to this equality, compose with $\epsilon_{h',Lv^*K}$, and substitute the displayed mate identity. Naturality of $B$ then gives
$$t_{h',Lv^*K}Rh'_!(b_K)B_{S_hK}=Lv^*(t_{h,K}).$$
This is the required base-change square for the smooth trace. Apply it to $h=f,g,gf$ in the base-changed pair of composable morphisms; the transitivity formula already proved holds for that pair as well. The proof uses no flatness or smoothness of $v$. For geometric fibers of structural affine space the trace and its class are the pulled-back arrows, as in Step 3; compact-support exchange exists for arbitrary base change, so no finite-type hypothesis on the geometric-point field is inserted. A purity-defined exchange alone would not establish the counit identity; the cited orientation/tensor factors are what relate it to the counit-normalized map.

source.place: Step 3: expand the counit-normalized base-change calculation

proof.text:
For finite reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ let $T_X,T_Y$ be derived scalar extension, $q:T_YF_A\cong F_BT_X$ the compact-support comparison and $b:T_XU_A\cong U_BT_Y$ its counit-normalized mate. The statement of [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons] gives
$$\epsilon_BF_B(b_K)=T_Y(\epsilon_{A,K})q_{U_AK}^{-1}.$$
Let $\lambda:T_XS_AK\cong S_BT_YK$ be the twist/pullback comparison. Purity reduction [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] gives $b_KT_X(\gamma_{A,K})=\gamma_{B,T_YK}\lambda$. Applying $F_B$, composing with the counit and using naturality of $q$ gives
$$t_{B,T_YK}F_B(\lambda)q_{S_AK}=T_Y(t_{A,K}).$$
This proves finite-reduction compatibility for the actual trace arrows, including their twists. The same reduction theorem includes the orientations and coherence squares. Applying the reduction functor to the transitivity equality and to the normalization equality therefore gives their reduced versions, with $1$ mapping to $1$.

source.place: Step 4: finite reduction, with its explicit counit identity

proof.text: For a normalized integral system $K=(K_n)_n$, [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] reconstructs the compatible purity maps, and [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] asserts the corresponding transport for the smooth trace and the composition and base-change coherences. Apply that transport to the actual finite-level traces of the preceding steps: it supplies the integral trace whose reductions are those maps. Composition of morphisms, identity morphisms and the distinguished unit classes are preserved by the reconstruction functor on the coherent systems. Thus the finite-level transitivity and normalization calculations become the same calculations in the integral category, and the base-change diagram is the transported one. This uses the stated trace-coherence transport, rather than an unsupported assertion that equality of arbitrary derived morphisms can be checked solely on separate finite reductions.

source.place: Step 4: integral trace and coherence transport

proof.text: Finally [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] identifies the field-coefficient purity maps with the rationalized and common-finite-stage integral maps, and [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence] gives the same identification for their smooth traces and composition/base-change coherences. Apply these functors to the integral trace equality, normalization and base-change square. They preserve composition, identities and the coefficient unit, so the images are exactly the asserted $E$- and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-statements. The common-stage trace compatibility makes the calculation independent of the lattice or finite coefficient field used to represent it. Together with Step 6 this establishes all coefficient transports named in the statement.

\end{array}
$$

where $\alpha_{g,f}$ is the composition law of
[thm-sf-comp-composition],
equals $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{gf,K}$, after the pullback-composition
and twist-additivity identifications; thus the $f$-trace, with the
$(e)[2e]$ twist already present, is applied before the $g$-trace.
On every geometric fiber of a structural $f=p_d:\mathbf A^d\to\Spec k$,
the smooth trace

$$
\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{p_d,\Lambda}:
R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^d,\Lambda(d)[2d])\longrightarrow\Lambda
$$

is the product of the normalized affine-line traces of
[thm-pur-affine-line-purity]: it sends the ordered fundamental class
of $\mathbf A^d$, the $d$-fold tensor of the affine-line classes, to
$1\in\Lambda$. The smooth traces are compatible with arbitrary base

proof.text:
Step 1: the transitivity. Expanding the two composites with
[def-pur-smooth-trace], the left-hand composite is

$$
\begin{gathered}
Rg_!Rf_!Lf^*Lg^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]
\\
\xrightarrow{\ Rg_!Rf_!(\gamma_{f,Lg^*K(e)[2e]})\ }
Rg_!Rf_!Rf^!Lg^*K(e)[2e]
\\
\xrightarrow{\ Rg_!(\operatorname{Tr}_{f,Lg^*K(e)[2e]})\ }
Rg_!Lg^*K(e)[2e]
\\
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{g,K}\ }K,
\end{gathered}
$$

where the first arrow is the $\alpha_{g,f}^{-1}$-identification of the
statement (the pullback-composition and twist-additivity identifications,
all canonical), and the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{f,Lg^*K(e)[2e]}$ is
the counit of $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ evaluated on $Lg^*K(e)[2e]$. The
transposed form of the purity–composition coherence
[thm-pur-composition-coherence] says that
$Rf_!(\gamma_{f,Lg^*K(e)[2e]})$ followed by the counit is the counit
of $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ applied to the object $Lf^*Lg^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]$
through the composition isomorphism $c_{g,f}$ – it identifies
$Rf_!Rf^!Lg^*K(e)[2e]$ with $Rf_!Lf^*Lg^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]$ – so the
composite of the last three displayed arrows is exactly the
$f$-trace $Rg_!(\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,Lg^*K(e)[2e]})$,
which is what the statement's composite applies. The remaining
identification is the functoriality of the counits with respect to the
canonical identification $R(gf)_!\cong Rg_!Rf_!$ (the $\alpha_{g,f}$
of [thm-sf-comp-composition]), the compatibility of the
adjunction with composition being the transpose of the composition
isomorphism of the $R^!$-side (the composition
isomorphism of the $R_!$-side is the transpose of the one of the
$R^!$-side, and the triangle identity of the adjunction
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ is used once, in the form
$\operatorname{Tr}_f\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K})=\operatorname{Tr}_{f,K}$).
Hence the two composites agree, which is the transitivity.
Step 2: the normalization on the geometric fiber. For
$f=p_d:\mathbf A^d\to\Spec k$, the smooth trace
$\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{p_d,\Lambda}$ is, by
[def-pur-smooth-trace], $R\Gamma_c(\gamma_{p_d,\Lambda})$ followed
by the counit, and by the agreement
[lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] the purity map
$\gamma_{p_d,\Lambda}$ is the affinity-space purity comparison, i.e. the affinity-space integration of
[cor-pur-affine-space-purity]; by induction on $d$ with Step 1
(the case $d+e$ with $e=1$: the $d$-fold trace is the iterate of
the one-fold trace), and with the case $d=1$ being
[thm-pur-affine-line-purity] in adjoint form (the
affine-line integration $\int_p$ of the orientation sends the
fundamental class of $\mathbf A^1$ to $1$, by the normalization of
the orientation in [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]), the trace
of the ordered fundamental class, the $d$-fold tensor of the
affine-line classes, is the product of the images, i.e.

$$
\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{p_d,\Lambda}\bigl(\underbrace{1\otimes\cdots\otimes1}\bigr)=1\in\Lambda;
$$

the intermediate Koszul signs in the reassociations are $+1$ by
[cor-pur-affine-space-purity] (the shift factors are of even
degree). Step 3: the base-change compatibility. The smooth trace is
compatible with the base change of $Z$ by the conjugation of
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence] with the compact-support
base change of the adjunctions (the trace is the counit, the counit of
the pulled-back adjunction is the pullback of the counit under the
base-change maps: the base-change compatibility of the adjunction
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$). Step 4: the coefficient
transport. The compatibility with finite reduction is the transport
of [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] (the trace is built from
the purity isomorphism and the counit, both reducing compatibly),
and the adic and rational transports are the corresponding
statements of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] and
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], which transport the smooth
trace together with the purity isomorphism.

split_report.summary: No exact attachment and no new nodes. Expanded the four blueprint tasks into eight typed proof steps, replaced the invalid triangle-identity argument by purity and counit naturality, proved rank-zero and ordered affine-space normalization, used the counit-normalized base-change factors rather than a purity-defined exchange alone, and cited the separate adic/rational trace-coherence companions. All levels n are retained by the existing extended projection-agreement interface.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 needs Lg^*K to remain bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude before evaluating the f-trace. This is a general domain-preservation fact; the transport unit does not supply its own pullback-preservation statement.

Step 1 evaluates gamma_f at Rg^!K and needs the constructible exceptional functor to preserve finite Tor amplitude. This is the general restriction theorem, not a replacement proof of a trace or coefficient-transport clause.

Step 4 uses the actual natural projection isomorphism for a shifted Tate-line coefficient to define and evaluate the ordered external product class. The transport unit has no separate finite-coefficient projection-formula theorem.

Step 5 requires compatibility of orientation and tensor map with the counit-normalized exceptional exchange. The same-unit smooth-base-change-coherence interface only supplies a square for a purity-defined exchange and cannot replace this comparison.
